summary: Feed s066_single to NDR is degraded: 20.6% of TCP sessions (35/170) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. NDR requires bidirectional traffic for stateful analysis. All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/feed is delivering only one direction for 20.6% of sessions. With no packet drops or tool overload detected, this is not loss/congestion but a visibility sourcing/aggregation issue: likely only one side of the path is tapped/SPANned, asymmetric routing is only partially captured, or broker is hashing client->server and server->client to different egress ports instead of aggregating both directions to this NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, session tracking, and request/response correlation. One-way flows cause broken flow records, missed detections, inaccurate anomaly scoring, and inability to detect lateral movement/C2 for affected 35 sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR egress port using bidirectional flow-aware hashing/aggregation so the NDR receives complete client-server conversations for stateful detection.
